audit_findings.title: Series A preferred claim is missing and its conversion dilution appears mis-scaled
audit_findings.magnitude: $50.0 million liquidation preference; $2.875 million annual preferred dividend; potential conversion cap of 3.4118 million common shares versus 0.003412 million reportedly included
audit_findings.mechanism: The liquidation preference reduces the equity bridge, preferred dividends reduce OE available to common holders, and any applicable conversion increases fully diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Moreover, holders of our depositary shares and outstanding preferred stock have preferential dividend and liquidation rights compared to holders of our common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The missing $50.0 million senior claim is demonstrated by the filed preferred-stock terms and the valuation bridge. It equals about $1.15 per currently modeled diluted share. The filing also shows that 2025 income applicable to common stockholders was reduced by $2.875 million of preferred dividends, but the OE record does not establish that this deduction was made. The reported conversion-share amount also appears mis-scaled by roughly 1,000 times, although conversion is contingent on a change of control and therefore should not be combined with a simultaneous liquidation-preference deduction.
audit_findings.action: Trace the OE starting-income line to the filed $310.350 million income applicable to common stockholders. Rerun the common-equity valuation using either a $50.0 million preferred-claim deduction with no conversion dilution or the correctly calculated change-of-control conversion treatment, without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Parent-attributable earnings may be mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.286 million 2025 difference between consolidated net income of $343.511 million and parent-attributable net income of $313.225 million, equal to 19.8% of the $153.3 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Mixing parent-only starting earnings with consolidated D&A, working-capital changes, capital expenditures and investment cash flows can misstate the OE anchor and therefore every projected cash flow and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The noncontrolling interest attributable to the 50% minority interest owned by TPG was included as noncontrolling interests in the Company’s consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the cash-flow statement is consolidated and that 2025 consolidated earnings exceeded parent-attributable earnings by $30.286 million. The record does not provide the OE worksheet needed to prove which consolidated adjustments were applied or their parent share. The mismatch could overstate or understate OE because consolidated noncash add-backs and consolidated reinvestment requirements can move in opposite directions, but the scale is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 OE line by line from parent-attributable earnings, allocating D&A, working capital, capital expenditures, unconsolidated-investment flows and cash consistently to GRBK common holders; then rerun all scenarios from the corrected anchor.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable noncontrolling interest is an unbridged common-equity claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $55.035 million carrying amount at June 30, 2026; $3.565 million minority income and $5.669 million distributions for the six months ended June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: A future put payment would reduce common-holder cash, while acquiring the remaining 20% interest would add the associated earnings; both sides must be modeled consistently in OE or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On March 23, 2023, the Company and the minority partner amended the operating agreement of GRBK GHO to change the start of the put and purchase options from April 2024 to April 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates a $55.035 million redeemable noncontrolling interest that is absent from the bridge, but it also reports that the put start was deferred to April 2030. Its carrying amount is about 2.3% of base equity value. Materiality cannot be established from that amount alone because the exercise price depends on future financial results and payment would acquire the minority earnings currently excluded from parent-attributable OE. The net value direction therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the amended put/call agreement and calculate the current formula-based redemption estimate. Model the present value of the expected purchase price together with the incremental parent-attributable OE acquired, then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Tax-payment timing may inflate the 2025 OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $43.451 million increase in federal income tax payable, equal to 28.3% of the $153.3 million OE anchor; 2025 tax expense was $94.667 million versus $50.111 million cash paid
audit_findings.mechanism: If the increase in taxes payable was included as an operating working-capital inflow, it raises the one-year OE anchor even though the accrued tax must subsequently be paid.
audit_findings.evidence: Income tax expense was $94.7 million for each of the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The tax-timing difference is demonstrated: federal income tax payable rose from $3.749 million to $47.200 million, accounting for essentially all of the reported $42.415 million consolidated increase in accrued expenses. What remains unresolved is whether the OE calculation included that accrued-expense inflow. If it did, the $43.451 million deferral is large relative to the anchor and is not sustainable recurring owner earnings.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $42.415 million accrued-expense cash-flow adjustment in the OE worksheet, remove the federal-tax-payable component, normalize taxes using filed tax expense or a sustainable cash tax rate, and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Added stake value may omit mandatory funding and guarantees
audit_findings.magnitude: $77.708 million stakes added; $119.5 million filed maximum exposure at June 30, 2026, including a $9.2 million Rainwater capital commitment and a $22.5 million Magnolia Ridge completion guarantee; remaining Rainwater development funding is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unmodeled capital commitments or probable guarantee payments reduce the additive value of unconsolidated stakes in the equity bridge unless the associated incremental asset value or cash flows are also recognized.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company’s maximum exposure to loss as a result from its involvement with Rainwater Crossing was approximately $ 61.1 million, representing its $51.5 million investment and the Company’s remaining commitment to contribute to the joint venture $9.6 million in quarterly payments through March 31, 2029.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge adds approximately the full filed carrying amount of the unconsolidated investments. The $9.2 million commitment is a demonstrated future funding requirement, while the $22.5 million guarantee is contingent rather than a demonstrated loss. Contributions may create corresponding venture value, and the record neither quantifies remaining Rainwater development funding nor establishes expected guarantee calls. Accordingly, the record cannot determine the net material effect, although omitted obligations could overstate the stake adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $77.708 million bridge amount by venture to carrying value and estimated realizable value; obtain remaining development budgets, commitment schedules and guarantee status; deduct only unfunded amounts not supported by incremental value or cash flows, and rerun the bridge.
